system: You are LocAgent, a graph-guided code-localization agent. Navigate the JavaScript code graph (function & file nodes; invokes / invoked_by / parent / child / event edges) to find the single behaviour-anchor function. This benchmark requires a submit tool call, not a prose answer. Prefer the function that constructs or returns the observed field/value over a nested encoder helper. The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behaviour chain: the earliest function (after routing and input preparation) whose own body constructs the target observable value, rather than collecting inputs, dispatching control, wrapping a result, or emitting it.

messages.content:
Task: Locate the anchor function for the media_fp field in the console.log object whose action is media.fingerprint after selecting the color profile, codec lane and render tier and clicking Probe fingerprint on the page. The anchor function is the first target-specific media fingerprint value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after action routing, stage gating, browser and media-capability signal collection, asynchronous hand-off, local event dispatch and per-stage folding, its function body itself constructs the target observable media fingerprint hash value rather than merely collecting browser/media environment signals, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, or writing to the console. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, raw signal collectors, or the final sink. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.

Example value: mf_iis3u0zbo0gr
Observable: {'type': 'console', 'api': 'console.log', 'action': 'media.fingerprint', 'field': 'media_fp'}
Candidate seed nodes (lexical prior, not a ranking): ['026b48d451f38e7b', 'c64e6d94d49dc5fb', '73896cd90240feb5', '35cb264487c944f1', 'a568baed34f00d52', 'f7c25d8bcc7abf61', '7c75fd92cffaaffe', '4ea8e18de37b297a']
Use search_entity / traverse_graph / retrieve_entity, then call submit with file, start_offset, and end_offset for ONE complete function.

tools.name: search_entity
tools.description: Find function/file nodes by keyword (matches name or body). Returns node ids.

tools.name: traverse_graph
tools.description: List neighbours of a function node along an edge type. edge in {invokes, invoked_by, parent, child, event}.

tools.name: retrieve_entity
tools.description: Return the full source and location of a function node id.

tools.name: submit
tools.description: Submit the single complete anchor function (file + offsets).
